title: Fog Descends
subtitle: This is not an ideal day for a drive, regardless of the vehicle.

trails.title: Tales and Journeys
trails.description: This magazine column was always popular, but now the columnist's trail has vanished near Route 77.

content.text:
Since our last column, we've been inundated with letters, tapes, and voice recordings from our passionate readers. I must say, the impact of the "Piranhas in the Sewers" story exceeded my expectations. One anonymous reader compiled 23 different urban sewer predator legends she picked up during her travels and asked when I was going to write about "The Country Witch Who Turned Into a Hare." She fondly recalled how her grandmother's amusing witch stories, tinged with a touch of gentle fright, would lull her to sleep as a child.

I'd like to extend my heartfelt thanks to this reader—these contributions are invaluable to my writing, and I'll soon delve into these childhood tales. Stories of mysterious transformative arcane skills are truly captivating, and their prevalence might be more widespread than I initially thought.

As we continue with the last issue's theme, sewer legends intertwine with conspiracy theories. For example, in a tape sent in by a Mr. K from New York City, a relative of his staunchly believes that the government secretly hired a team to feed albino fish living in the sewers. In previous investigations, a teenager shared his thrilling experience—he encountered human-sized, upright-walking reptiles and rodents in the city sewers. These stories often end with the line, "The government knows they exist, but the higher-ups are keeping it all hush-hush ..." More radical speculators suggest that city sewers can easily be used as experimentation sites, with piranhas, alligators, giant snakes, and all manner of other dangerous creatures being secretly bred by the government or mysterious organizations for unknown purposes.

...

In our next column, we'll be returning to Texas—where this series began. As you read this, I'll most likely already have set off on a new adventure. Perhaps our paths will cross on the dusty roads of Texas.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Before we left, TTT was telling me an urban myth about Texas.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hah. Sounds about right. What's the story about?
The story starts off in the typical way.
A man was driving down a long Texas road when he saw a girl hitch-hiking.
He offered her a lift and a piece of chocolate.
The man dropped the girl off at a cemetery and drove on. It was late at night, so he was hoping to reach his destination quickly.
Soon after, he saw a funeral procession going down the road.
The photo of the dead seemed familiar.
Curiosity came over him, and he followed them to the cemetery.
Look, a piece of chocolate.
A sudden beeping interrupts her story.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Give me a moment. I have to take this. It's from the Foundation.
The voice on the other side is as calm as ever.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Timekeeper, this is an emergency notice. The Zeno Base in Texas, USA, has conducted a large-scale evacuation.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Zeno has not yet responded regarding their actions.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Should you encounter any difficulties on your trip there, please contact headquarters immediately.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Understood.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Despite these developments, your mission remains the same.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Contact UTTU editor Barbara, who was last seen near Route 77 collecting information, and find Urd's current whereabouts through her.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Since UTTU editors use a special communication channel, her current location is still unknown. We'll be in touch as soon as there's any new information.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: Any questions, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. Thank you.

items.speaker: Communicator
items.text: All the best, then.
The communication ends. Lilya looks thoughtful.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What did they say?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There was a mass evacuation at the Zeno base in Texas.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Tsk. What's that all about?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They called me two days ago, saying that Red 38 was still under routine maintenance in their armament factory.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But now, all of a sudden, they're gone? How am I going to get my Red 38 back now, huh?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If they hadn't taken her away for inspection, we wouldn't be traveling in this little car, wasting all day on the road.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The operator only mentioned an evacuation. It's still possible that some of them have stayed behind to keep the factory running.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If you're worried about Red 38, we can take a detour there. It's in Chisos. The town isn't far from here.
Lilya squirms in her seat.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hey, mister, can you take us to the Chisos? It's just a little detour.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Hmm.
He taps his fingers rhythmically on the steering wheel.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Girls, I don't know why y'all are here. But whether it's just for a bit of adventure or for business, I gotta tell you. Something ain't right in that town.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: We've all heard the stories—scratching sounds on car roofs, animal bits stuck to car grilles, and those people in black robes running around. It's all too weird for me.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ah, give the ghost stories a rest.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Look, if you're trying to negotiate a higher price, at least be a little smart about it instead of trying to spook us with a few tall tales.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: You got me all wrong. Who in their right mind would throw away the cash in their hand unless they were forced to?

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Benjamins are good and all, but they ain't worth my life. Ain't no way I'm taking you there, no matter how much cash you throw at me.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Why? Were you the driver in that ghost story?

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: N-No.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Have you seen these things happen yourself?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Come on, it's just a little detour! It won't even cost you much fuel!
He clenches his hands tightly around the steering wheel, his knuckles turning white from the pressure.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sir?

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: You see that? It's fogging up.
Thick, milky fog envelopes the car.
The driver pulls over.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Ain't no way this fog is natural. We shouldn't go any further. I'm stopping right here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ugh, fine, I'll drive. Swap seats with me.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: No. Nobody get out of the car.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Are you kidding me?! You haven't heard the stories, have you? Then what in the hell are you even doing here?!

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: When the fog rolls in on Route 77, you should always stay in the car. All kinds of terrible things hide in the fog. Some folks say they saw giant white crocodiles; others say they saw dead bodies hanging from trees.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Ain't nobody leaving this car. Not until the fog's gone.
*screech*
He's interrupted by a drawn-out scraping sound on the roof of the car.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Is that ... Is that ...?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, come on! Don't tell me you're scared of this stuff!
No response.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He's fainted.
A strange atmosphere spreads inside the car as they sit and listen to the scraping on the roof. But this is nothing compared to what happened at Green Lake Campsite.
Finally, the scraping stops, and a few black-and-white figures dart past the windows.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. This looks like the work of a Mummus. It's a critter commonly seen in the southern US. When they're frightened, they produce a fog-like gas from their respiratory trumpet.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So that sound is just some critter scratching along on the roof.
Lilya opens the door.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: At this rate, I won't get my Red 38 back for another month!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Well, I've always wanted to try this. Help me move this guy! And you'll have to give up your passenger seat, Captain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I know what you're thinking. But do you have a US driver's license? Or any driver's license at all, for that matter?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What do I need that for? I can fly a broom and even do all those maneuvers. That takes more skill than driving a car, don't you think?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ha, compared to flying, driving a car is child's play. Just look at the number of drivers compared to pilots in the world.
Following the pilot's plan, they adjust positions.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Now, where do we start?
She glances at the dashboard in front of her.
This doesn't look like the interior of an Su-01ве. A minor issue.
She thinks back to her training.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Start both engines. Keep the tachometer at 70%.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Here's the nose wheel steering, the position indicator for the joystick, the throttle lever ... ah, and these are for the flaps.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: No, no! That's not right! We're in a car, not a flying machine!
*click*
The rear-seat passenger quietly fastens her seatbelt.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Let's just get out, Captain. Can't wrap my head around this hunk of metal.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good decision.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If these critters are responsible for this fog, our solution is simple. We drive them away.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Let's go.
She opens the door, and the thick fog outside rushes in like a tide.
